clue.text: Land in America and disperse

definitions.meaning: in American usage a large ranch or farm is called a ...

explanation.surface: Settlers arrive in America and then go their separate ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a spread in US English, and scattering something widely also means spreading it.

clue.text: Touchy and old, under pressure, snap

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces sit under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
hot can mean touchy, as in a hot topic

explanation.surface: A tetchy old man under stress snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a snapshot, a quickly taken photograph.

clue.text: In English firm, I'm worthy of deep respect

indicators.note: the contraction goes in the combined English and firm

parts.note: stable means firm, steady
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone at an English company boasts of being highly respected.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving esteem, worthy of high regard.

clue.text: One churchman or another holding firm

indicators.note: the other cleric holds the firm inside him

parts.note: another churchman, a dean heads a cathedral chapter
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: One cleric or a second one owns a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister of the church ranking below a priest.

clue.text: Make flattering comments in indulgent TV programme

parts.note: an indulgent parent is soft, lenient
a soap is a soap opera on television

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cosy, undemanding television show.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap is to win someone over with flattery, an idiom from smoothing things over.

clue.text: Disaster one can't blame on other party

definitions.text: Disaster one can't blame on other party

parts.words: Disaster one can't blame on other party
parts.note: a catastrophe brought about by oneself, so nobody else is at fault

explanation.surface: A politician laments a fiasco that cannot be pinned on the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-destruction is ruin brought on by oneself, so there is no one else to blame.

clue.text: Quickly dispatched rations for the fleet?

definitions.text: Quickly dispatched rations for the fleet?

parts.words: Quickly dispatched rations for the fleet?
parts.note: meals served in a hurry, or whimsically provisions for those who are fleet, swift

explanation.surface: Supplies are rushed out to the navy's ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' means ships, but also fast, and food for the fleet is food for the fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast food is quickly prepared and served meals, eaten on the go.

clue.text: Jump off

explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden jump of surprise, and the start of a race is the off.

clue.text: Greek king, soon securing match, married

indicators.note: the word for soon secures, holds, the other pieces inside it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
a game is a match

explanation.surface: A Greek monarch will shortly make a match and wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks against Troy.

clue.text: Service problems resulting from crossed lines

definitions.text: Service problems resulting from crossed lines

parts.words: Service problems resulting from crossed lines
parts.note: reads like a telephone fault, but in tennis a server who steps over the baseline while serving is penalised

explanation.surface: A phone service is plagued by crossed lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the server is faulted when a foot crosses the baseline during the serve.

clue.text: Time excluded from world records, unfortunately

indicators.note: something excluded is left out, so one letter is removed from the book

parts.note: an atlas is a book recording the world in maps

explanation.surface: Time has been left out of the record books, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used just like 'sadly' or 'more's the pity'.

clue.text: News about maiden taken to court produces bitterness

indicators.note: the word for news goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: word can mean news, as in 'send word'

to court a lover is to woo them

explanation.surface: Reports of a young woman taken to court cause resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood is a proverbially bitter plant, so the word stands for bitterness or grief.

clue.text: Articles carried by French priest

indicators.note: the articles are held inside the abbreviation, carried within it

parts.note: a and the are the two English articles

explanation.surface: Some items are being transported by a French clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the title of a Catholic or Anglican priest.

clue.text: Old-fashioned art, for example, in extremely short book

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: Antique art is crammed into a very brief volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' here is not painting but the archaic 'thou art', a form of 'to be'. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Art' is an old form of the verb 'to be', so it is an example of a doing word.

clue.text: Mysteries, including a secret I spread around inner circle

indicators.note: the scattered letters go around the circle, which ends up inner

clue.text: Depositing about a thousand, so making charges

clue.text: Kills rival after service

clue.text: Declare antique, having done statistical calculation

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: An expert pronounces a piece old after doing the sums.

clue.text: Besides, you can continue on the next page

explanation.surface: A footnote tells the reader there is more to read overleaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover means in addition, and 'more over' tells a reader to turn the page.

clue.text: Lied as child before finally confessing

clue.text: Vessel, say, south of cape

clue.text: Facial protection for a tree-feller

clue.text: Make overt change, as supporter of politician

clue.text: Combine around NATO member in determined way

clue.text: Clue that produces suspicion

clue.text: Celebrities not altogether complimentary about new title

clue.text: Bossy old woman's husband I had seen in Scottish island
